title.zh: 卷一百二十 志第七十三 禮二十三
title.raw: 卷一百二十 志第七十三 禮二十三 Volume 120 Treatises 73: Rites 23

sentences.zh: 群臣上表儀宰臣赴上儀朝省集議班位臣僚上馬之制臣僚呵引之制

translations.literal: Rites for the multitude of ministers presenting memorials; rites for chief ministers presenting themselves at court; seating for assemblies at the provincial offices; regulations for officials mounting horses; regulations for ushering and announcing officials.
translations.idiomatic: On the rites for ministers presenting memorials, for chief ministers reporting to court, for seating at provincial assemblies, for officials mounting horses, and for ushering officials along the route.

sentences.zh: 群臣上表儀。

translations.literal: Rites for the multitude of ministers presenting memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for ministers presenting memorials.

sentences.zh: 《通禮》：守宮設次於朝堂，文東武西，相對為首設中書令位於群臣之北。

translations.literal: According to the Comprehensive Rites: the palace attendants set up stations in the audience hall, civil officials to the east and military to the west, facing each other as the head; the position of the Director of the Secretariat was set north of the multitude of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Rites prescribe that palace attendants arrange stations in the audience hall, with civil officials east and military west, facing one another at the head of the formation, and the Director of the Secretariat's place set north of the assembled ministers.

sentences.zh: 禮曹掾舉表案入，引中書令出，就南面立。

translations.literal: A clerk of the Rites Bureau raised the memorial case and entered, leading the Director of the Secretariat out to stand facing south.
translations.idiomatic: A Rites Bureau clerk carried in the memorial case, escorted the Director of the Secretariat forth, and had him stand facing south.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎中取表授中書令，令即受表入奏。

translations.literal: A director of the Ministry of Rites took the memorial and handed it to the Director of the Secretariat; the Director immediately received the memorial and entered to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: A Ministry of Rites director took the memorial and presented it to the Director of the Secretariat, who at once received it and went in to present it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其禮：凡正、至不受朝，及邦國大慶瑞、上尊號請舉行大禮，宰相率文武群臣暨諸軍將校、蕃夷酋長、道釋、耆老等詣東上閣門拜表，知表官跪授表於宰臣，宰臣跪授於閣門使，乃由通進司奏禦。

translations.literal: The rite: whenever on the winter and summer solstices the court did not receive audience, and on great felicitations and auspicious omens for the state, or when petitioning to confer an honorific title and request the performance of a great ceremony, the chief minister would lead the civil and military multitude of ministers together with military officers of the various armies, chieftains of foreign tribes, Daoist and Buddhist clergy, and elders, and so on, to proceed to the eastern upper Gatehouse to kowtow and present a memorial; the official in charge of the memorial would kneel and hand the memorial to the chief minister, the chief minister would kneel and hand it to the Gatehouse commissioner, and then it would be memorialized to the emperor through the Memorial Submission Office.
translations.idiomatic: The procedure was as follows: on the solstices, when the court did not hold audience, and whenever the realm celebrated a major auspicious event, or when ministers petitioned to bestow an honorific title and perform a grand ceremony, the chief minister led civil and military officials together with army commanders, tribal chieftains, Daoist and Buddhist clergy, and elders to the eastern upper Gatehouse to kowtow and submit a memorial. The memorial officer knelt and passed the document to the chief minister, who knelt and handed it to the Gatehouse commissioner; the Memorial Submission Office then presented it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 凡有答詔，亦拜受於閣門，獲可，奏者奉表稱賀。

translations.literal: Whenever there was an imperial response edict, one also kowtowed and received it at the Gatehouse; once approval was granted, the presenter would hold the memorial and offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial reply arrived, recipients likewise kowtowed to receive it at the Gatehouse; once approval was granted, the presenter held up the memorial and offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 其正、至，樞密使率內班拜表長春殿門外，亦閣門使受之。

translations.literal: On the solstices, the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs would lead the inner guard to kowtow and present a memorial outside the Changchun Hall gate, and the Gatehouse commissioner would also receive it.
translations.idiomatic: On the solstices, the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner led the inner guard in kowtowing and presenting a memorial outside the Changchun Hall gate, which the Gatehouse commissioner likewise received.

sentences.zh: 又西京留守拜表儀制：留司百官每五日一上表起居，質明，並集長壽寺立班，置表於案，再拜以遣。

translations.literal: Further, the rites for the Western Capital guardian presenting a memorial: the officials left behind in the capital every five days presented a memorial on imperial well-being; at dawn they all assembled at Changshou Temple to form ranks, placed the memorial on a table, and sent it off with two bows.
translations.idiomatic: There were also rites for the Western Capital guardian's memorial: every five days the officials remaining in the capital submitted a memorial on the emperor's well-being. At daybreak they assembled at Changshou Temple in formation, set the memorial on a table, and dispatched it with two bows.

sentences.zh: 其春、秋賜服及大慶瑞並如之。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn bestowals of robes and great felicitations and auspicious omens were all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and autumn distributions of court robes, as well as major celebrations and auspicious omens, followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 或令分司官齎詣行在，或止驛付南京留司，約用此制。

translations.literal: Sometimes branch-office officials were ordered to carry it to the traveling palace, or it was left at a relay station for delivery to the Nanjing officials left behind, approximately using this system.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes branch-office officials were ordered to carry the memorial to the traveling court, or it was left at a courier station for the Nanjing remnant staff—roughly following this system.

sentences.zh: 若巡幸，東京則留司百官亦五日一上表起居，並集大相國寺。

translations.literal: If the emperor toured, then in the Eastern Capital the officials left behind also every five days presented a memorial on well-being, all assembling at Daxiangguo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was on tour, officials remaining in the Eastern Capital likewise submitted a well-being memorial every five days, assembling at Daxiangguo Temple.

sentences.zh: 其制：群臣詣閣拜奏者，首雲文武百僚具官臣某等言；

translations.literal: The regulation: when the multitude of ministers proceeded to the Gatehouse to kowtow and memorialize, the opening would read, 'The civil and military hundred officials, officials of full rank, your subjects So-and-so and others state';
translations.idiomatic: The rule for ministers kowtowing and presenting memorials at the Gatehouse required an opening such as, 'The civil and military officials of full rank, your subjects So-and-so and others respectfully state';

sentences.zh: 常奏禦者，止雲臣某言，並稱尊號，已有功臣爵邑者具之；

translations.literal: for regular memorials to the emperor, one only said, 'Your subject So-and-so states,' and also used the honorific title; those who already held noble ranks and fiefs would list them;
translations.idiomatic: for routine presentations to the throne, the opener was simply, 'Your subject So-and-so states,' together with the emperor's honorific title, and any existing noble rank or fief was listed;

sentences.zh: 狀奏者，前後列銜，不稱尊號，亦雲功臣爵邑。

translations.literal: for memorials in the form of a report, offices were listed before and after, the honorific title was not used, but noble ranks and fiefs were also stated.
translations.idiomatic: for formal reports, titles were listed fore and aft without the honorific title, though noble ranks and fiefs were still recorded.

sentences.zh: 其外，又有書疏、奏劄、榜子之類。

translations.literal: Beyond these, there were also letters, memorial notes, and placard-style submissions.
translations.idiomatic: Besides these forms, there were also letters, folded memorial notes, and placard-style submissions.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，令有司詳定表首。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, an order was issued for the relevant offices to examine and fix the opening of memorials in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande (964), the throne ordered the relevant offices to review and fix the standard opening lines of memorials.

sentences.zh: 太常禮院言：「僕射南省官品第二，太子三師官品第一，品位雖高，而南省上臺為尊，合以僕射充首。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices Rites Office stated: 'The Vice Directors of the Secretariat hold official rank of the second degree in the Southern Administration, while the Three Preceptors of the Heir Apparent hold rank of the first degree; although their rank is higher, the superior platform of the Southern Administration is the more honored, and it is fitting that the Vice Director serve as head.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices Rites Office argued: 'Vice Directors of the Secretariat are second-rank officials of the Southern Administration, whereas the Heir Apparent's Three Preceptors are first rank; although their rank is higher, the superior platform of the Southern Administration takes precedence, so the Vice Director should lead the memorial.

sentences.zh: 若專以品秩為定，則諸行侍郎品第四，列于諸司三品卿監之上，不可以品序為准。

translations.literal: If one took rank alone as the standard, then the various bureau vice directors of the fourth rank would be placed above the third-rank directors and commissioners of the various offices, and rank order could not be used as the criterion.
translations.idiomatic: If rank alone were decisive, fourth-rank bureau vice directors would stand above third-rank directors and commissioners of other agencies—rank could not be the sole criterion.

sentences.zh: 按唐貞元六年詔，每有慶賀及諸臣上表，併合上公為首，如三公闕，以令、僕行之。

translations.literal: According to the edict of the sixth year of Zhenyuan in Tang, whenever there were congratulations and when the multitude of ministers presented memorials, they were jointly to take the senior lord as head; if the Three Dukes were vacant, the Director and Vice Directors would act.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang edict of the sixth year of Zhenyuan (790), whenever the court celebrated or ministers submitted memorials, the senior lord was to lead; if no Three Duke held office, the Director and Vice Directors of the Secretariat acted in his place.

sentences.zh: 中書、門下列貢章表，則僕射是百僚師長，難同宮僚之例。」

translations.literal: For the Secretariat and Chancellery submitting tribute memorials, the Vice Director was the chief of the hundred officials and could not be treated like palace staff.'
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat and Chancellery submitted tribute memorials, the Vice Director, as chief among the hundred officials, could not be classed with palace staff.'

sentences.zh: 詔百官集議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the hundred officials to assemble for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered the hundred officials to assemble and deliberate.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士陶谷等曰：「按唐制：上臺、東宮並是廷臣，當時左右僕射、侍中、中書令為正宰相。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Tao Gu and others said: 'According to Tang regulations: the superior platform and the Eastern Palace were both court officials; at that time the Left and Right Vice Directors, the Attendant-in-Chief, and the Director of the Secretariat were the true chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Tao Gu and others argued: 'Under Tang rules, both the superior platform and the Eastern Palace counted as court officials; at that time the Left and Right Vice Directors, the Attendant-in-Chief, and the Director of the Secretariat were the true chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 貞觀末，帶同中書門下三品者方為宰相。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenguan era, only those bearing the concurrent title of Same Rank as the Secretariat and Chancellery Third Rank were regarded as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Zhenguan era, only those who concurrently held the title Same Rank as the Secretariat and Chancellery Third Rank were counted as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 今僕射既非宰相，合在大子三師之下，理固不疑。

translations.literal: Today the Vice Director is no longer a chief minister and should rank below the Three Preceptors of the Heir Apparent; the principle admits no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Vice Director is no longer a chief minister and should stand below the Heir Apparent's Three Preceptors—a conclusion that follows necessarily.

sentences.zh: 若以宮僚非廷臣，既宰相豈當兼領？

translations.literal: If palace staff are not court officials, how could chief ministers concurrently hold such posts?
translations.idiomatic: If palace staff were not court officials, how could chief ministers hold such posts concurrently?

sentences.zh: 今若先二品而後一品，升後列而退前班，紊其等威，事恐非順。

translations.literal: If now one places second rank before first rank, promoting the rear row and demoting the front rank, this would disorder their precedence and dignity, and the affair would likely not be proper.
translations.idiomatic: To place second rank before first, advancing the rear row while demoting the front, would disorder precedence and dignity and would likely be improper.

sentences.zh: 請以太子三師為表首。」

translations.literal: We request that the Three Preceptors of the Heir Apparent serve as the head of the memorial.'
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the Heir Apparent's Three Preceptors lead the memorial.'

sentences.zh: 竇儀等曰：「東宮三師為表首，論討故典，實皆無據。

translations.literal: Dou Yi and others said: 'Taking the Eastern Palace Three Preceptors as the head of the memorial, when one discusses and examines ancient precedents, in truth none supports it.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi and others replied: 'Making the Eastern Palace Three Preceptors lead the memorial has no real support in precedent when one examines the ancient regulations.

sentences.zh: 左右僕射當為表首者，其事有六：按《六典》，尚書為百官之本，今自一品至六品常參官，皆以尚書省官為首，則僕射合為表首，一也。

translations.literal: That the Left and Right Vice Directors should be the head of the memorial has six grounds: according to the Six Offices, the Department of State Affairs is the root of the hundred officials; today from first rank through sixth rank, all regular attendees take officials of the Department of State Affairs as head, so the Vice Director should be head—first.
translations.idiomatic: That the Left and Right Vice Directors should lead has six grounds. First, the Six Offices treat the Department of State Affairs as the root of the bureaucracy; from first through sixth rank, regular attendees all take Department officials as head, so the Vice Director should lead.

sentences.zh: 又唐制，上表無上公，即尚書令僕以下行之，其嗣王合隨宗正，若有班位，合依王品，則嗣王雖一品，不得為表首，二也。

translations.literal: Further, under Tang regulations, when presenting a memorial with no senior lord, it was the Director and Vice Directors of the Secretariat and below who acted; an heir of a princely house should follow the Court of the Imperial Clan, and if there were a place in the formation, it should follow princely rank—thus even if an heir of a princely house were first rank, he could not be head—second.
translations.idiomatic: Second, under Tang rules, when no senior lord led a memorial, the Secretariat Director and Vice Directors did so; imperial clansmen followed the Imperial Clan Court and, where they had a place in formation, took rank according to princely status—so even a first-rank imperial prince could not lead.

sentences.zh: 僕射位次三公，合為表首，三也。

translations.literal: The Vice Director's place follows the Three Dukes and he should be head—third.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the Vice Director ranks immediately after the Three Dukes and should therefore lead.

sentences.zh: 況僕射為百僚師長，東宮三師非師長之任，四也。

translations.literal: Moreover the Vice Director is chief among the hundred officials, while the Eastern Palace Three Preceptors are not a chief's duty—fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the Vice Director is chief among the hundred officials, whereas the Eastern Palace Three Preceptors do not hold a chieftain's role.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中詔，謝賀上表，上公行之，如闕，即令僕射行之，五也。

translations.literal: In the edict of the Tianfu era of Jin, for memorials of thanks and congratulations, the senior lord acted; if vacant, then the Director and Vice Directors acted—fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, a Jin edict of the Tianfu era required the senior lord to lead thanks and congratulatory memorials, with the Director and Vice Directors acting if he were absent.

sentences.zh: 立制之班，卑者先入後出，尊者後入先出。

translations.literal: In formations established by regulation, the lower enter first and leave last; the higher enter last and leave first.
translations.idiomatic: In regulated formations, the lower in rank enter first and leave last, while the higher enter last and leave first.

sentences.zh: 今東宮一品立定，僕射乃入，僕射既退，東宮一品乃出，且在兩省之後，六也。」

translations.literal: Today the Eastern Palace first rank stands fixed, then the Vice Director enters; after the Vice Director withdraws, the Eastern Palace first rank leaves—and moreover behind the two administrations—sixth.'
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, today the Eastern Palace first rank takes position first, then the Vice Director enters; after the Vice Director withdraws, the Eastern Palace first rank departs—and does so only after the two administrations.'

sentences.zh: 詔從儀等議，以僕射為表首焉。

translations.literal: An edict followed the deliberation of Yi and the others, taking the Vice Director as head of the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted Dou Yi and his colleagues' view and decreed that the Vice Director should lead memorials.

sentences.zh: 宰臣赴上儀。

translations.literal: Rites for chief ministers presenting themselves at court.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for chief ministers reporting to court.

sentences.zh: 《開元禮》有任官初上相見之儀。

translations.literal: The Kaiyuan Rites contain the ceremony for an official on first taking office to present himself and be received.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan Rites prescribe the ceremony by which a newly appointed official presents himself and is received.

sentences.zh: 宋制：凡牧守赴上，多仍州府舊禮。

translations.literal: Song regulations: whenever prefects and guardians presented themselves at court, they mostly retained the old rites of their prefecture or circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song rules, prefects and circuit guardians reporting to court generally kept their former prefectural or circuit ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 台省之制，宰相、親王、使相正衙謝訖，出文德殿便門至西廊，堂後官、兩省雜事迎參；

translations.literal: Regulations of the Secretariat and Chancellery: after the chief minister, imperial prince, or commissioner with chief-minister status had completed thanks in the main audience hall, he went out through the side gate of Wende Hall to the western corridor, where the rear-hall officials and clerks of the two administrations came forward to receive him;
translations.idiomatic: For the Secretariat and Chancellery: after a chief minister, imperial prince, or commissioner with chief-minister standing finished thanks in the main hall, he exited through Wende Hall's side gate to the western corridor, where rear-hall officials and clerks of the two administrations came out to receive him;

sentences.zh: 至中書便門，兩省官迎班；

translations.literal: upon reaching the side gate of the Secretariat, officials of the two administrations formed a welcoming line;
translations.idiomatic: at the Secretariat side gate, officials of the two administrations formed a welcoming line;

sentences.zh: 升都堂，與送上官對揖見任侍中、中書令、同平章事者

translations.literal: ascending to the main hall, he exchanged bows with the presenting superior facing one another, with the incumbent Attendant-in-Chief, Director of the Secretariat, or Commissioner with the title Equal in Authority to the Chief Minister
translations.idiomatic: ascending to the main hall, he exchanged facing bows with the presenting superior—the incumbent Attendant-in-Chief, Director of the Secretariat, or Commissioner Equal in Authority to the Chief Minister

sentences.zh: ，降階，又與送上官對拜訖，分東、西升坐於床。

translations.literal: , descending the steps, again exchanging facing bows with the presenting superior until finished, then separately ascending east and west to sit on the couch.
translations.idiomatic: , then descended the steps and exchanged facing bows again with the presenting superior; when finished, he and the superior took seats on the east and west couches respectively.

sentences.zh: 兩省雜事讀案，堂後官接案。

translations.literal: Clerks of the two administrations read the cases, and rear-hall officials received them.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks of the two administrations read out the cases, which rear-hall officials received.

sentences.zh: 搢笏頂筆判署，凡三道：一，司天監壽星見；

translations.literal: Inserting the tablet and holding the brush to the forehead, he marked approval—three items in all: first, the Directorate of Astronomy reported the Longevity Star appeared;
translations.idiomatic: He inserted his tablet and, brush held to his forehead, marked approval on three items: first, the Directorate of Astronomy reported the appearance of the Longevity Star;

sentences.zh: 二，開封府嘉禾合穗；

translations.literal: second, the Kaifeng prefecture reported auspicious grain with joined ears;
translations.idiomatic: second, Kaifeng prefecture reported auspicious grain with conjoined ears;

sentences.zh: 三，澶州黃河清。

translations.literal: third, the Yellow River at Dazhou ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: third, the Yellow River at Dazhou ran clear.

sentences.zh: 並判准，始謝送上官，訖，三司使、學士、兩省官、待制、三司副使升堂展賀。

translations.literal: All were marked approved; only then did he thank the presenting superior; when finished, the Commissioner of the Three Departments, academicians, officials of the two administrations, recipients of the title 'Awaiting Imperial Orders,' and vice commissioners of the Three Departments ascended the hall to extend congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: After marking all three approved, he thanked the presenting superior; then the Three Departments commissioner, Hanlin academicians, officials of the two administrations, holders of Awaiting Imperial Orders, and Three Departments vice commissioners ascended to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 百官先班中書門外，上事官降階，百官入，直省官通班贊致賀，歸後堂，與參知政事、樞密副使、宣徽使相見，會食訖，退。

translations.literal: The hundred officials first formed ranks outside the Secretariat gate; the official presenting himself at court descended the steps, the hundred officials entered, and the direct provincial official announced congratulations for the whole rank; returning to the rear hall, he met the Vice Commissioner for Participation in Governance, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, dined together until finished, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials first formed ranks outside the Secretariat gate. When the presenting official descended, they entered; a direct provincial clerk announced congratulations for the whole formation. He then returned to the rear hall to meet the Vice Commissioner for Participation in Governance, the Bureau of Military Affairs vice commissioner, and the Palace Domestic Service commissioner, shared a meal, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，中書、門下言：「准唐天成元年詔故事，藩鎮帶平章事，合於都堂視事，刊石以記官族，輸禮錢三千貫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong, the Secretariat and Chancellery stated: 'According to the precedent edict of the first year of Tiancheng in Tang, when a frontier commissioner held the title Equal in Authority to the Chief Minister, he should conduct affairs in the main hall, carve stone to record his official lineage, and pay a ceremonial gift of three thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong (962), the Secretariat and Chancellery reported: 'Under the Tang precedent of the first year of Tiancheng (926), a frontier commissioner who held Equal in Authority to the Chief Minister was to conduct business in the main hall, have his lineage carved in stone, and pay three thousand strings of cash as a ceremonial gift.

sentences.zh: 近年頗隳曩制。

translations.literal: In recent years the former system has been largely abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years that older system had largely fallen into disuse.

sentences.zh: 自今藩鎮帶平章事者，輸禮錢五百千，刻石記歲月。

translations.literal: From now on, frontier commissioners holding Equal in Authority to the Chief Minister shall pay five hundred thousand in ceremonial cash and have stone carved to record the year and month.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth frontier commissioners with that title were to pay five hundred thousand in ceremonial cash and have the year and month carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 其錢以給兩省公用，望舉行之。」

translations.literal: The money is to supply the common expenses of the two administrations; we hope it may be implemented.'
translations.idiomatic: The funds were to cover shared expenses of the two administrations; they asked that the rule be put into effect.'

sentences.zh: 詔自今宰相及樞密使兼平章事、侍中、中書令者，輸禮錢三百千，藩鎮五百千，刻石以記如舊制。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that from now on chief ministers and commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs concurrently holding Equal in Authority to the Chief Minister, Attendants-in-Chief, and Directors of the Secretariat should pay three hundred thousand in ceremonial cash, frontier commissioners five hundred thousand, with stone carved to record as in the old system.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: henceforth chief ministers and Bureau commissioners concurrently holding that title, Attendants-in-Chief, and Directors of the Secretariat were to pay three hundred thousand, frontier commissioners five hundred thousand, with stone records as before.

sentences.zh: 增秩者不再輸，舊相復入者輸如其數。

translations.literal: Those promoted in rank did not pay again; former chief ministers re-entering paid the same amount.
translations.idiomatic: Those promoted in rank did not pay again; former chief ministers returning to office paid the full amount anew.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，置參知政事，就宣徽院赴上，而樞密使、副止上事於本廳。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, Vice Commissioners for Participation in Governance were established; they presented themselves at the Palace Domestic Service courtyard, while the commissioner and vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs only presented themselves at their own bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande, Vice Commissioners for Participation in Governance were established; they reported to court at the Palace Domestic Service courtyard, while the Bureau commissioner and vice commissioner reported only within their own bureau.

sentences.zh: 後以曹彬兼侍中，為樞密使，特令赴中書上事。

translations.literal: Later, because Cao Bin concurrently held Attendant-in-Chief and served as Bureau commissioner, he was specially ordered to present himself at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because Cao Bin concurrently held Attendant-in-Chief while serving as Bureau commissioner, he was specially ordered to report at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，詔自今宰相官至僕射者，並於中書都堂赴上，不帶平章事亦令赴上。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong Xiangfu era, an edict ordered that from now on chief ministers down to the rank of Vice Director should all present themselves at the main hall of the Secretariat, and even those not holding Equal in Authority to the Chief Minister were also ordered to present themselves.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong Xiangfu era, an edict required all officials from chief minister down to Vice Director to report at the Secretariat main hall, including those without the concurrent chief-minister title.

sentences.zh: 有司上儀注，宰相用常儀。

translations.literal: The relevant offices submitted ritual regulations; chief ministers used the regular ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices submitted ritual protocols; chief ministers followed the regular ceremony.

sentences.zh: 僕射本省上日，郎中、員外班迎于都堂門內，尚書丞、郎於東廊階上稍近班迎揖，金吾將軍升殿展拜賀，禮生贊引，主事讀案。

translations.literal: On the day a Vice Director presented himself at his own department, directors and vice directors formed a welcoming line inside the main-hall gate; the department's assistant directors and directors on the eastern corridor steps formed a nearer welcoming line with bows; the Golden Guard general ascended the hall to extend bows of congratulation; ritual ushers guided; the chief clerk read the cases.
translations.idiomatic: On a Vice Director's departmental reporting day, directors and vice directors formed a welcoming line inside the main-hall gate; assistant directors and directors on the eastern corridor steps formed a nearer line and bowed; the Golden Guard general ascended to offer congratulatory bows; ritual ushers guided; the chief clerk read the cases.

sentences.zh: 見任中書樞密使相、前任中書門下並不赴，余如宰相之儀。

translations.literal: Incumbent Secretariat and Bureau chief ministers and former Secretariat and Chancellery officials did not attend; the rest followed the chief minister's ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Incumbent Secretariat and Bureau chief ministers and former Secretariat and Chancellery officials did not attend; the remainder followed the chief minister's rites.

sentences.zh: 上訖，與本省御史台四品、兩省五品、諸司三品以上會食。

translations.literal: When presentation was finished, he dined together with fourth-rank officials of his department and the Censorate, fifth-rank officials of the two administrations, and third-rank officials of the various offices and above.
translations.idiomatic: After reporting, he dined with fourth-rank officials of his department and the Censorate, fifth-rank officials of the two administrations, and third-rank officials of other agencies and above.

sentences.zh: 右僕射王旦充玉清昭應宮使，有司按故事，宰相凡有吉慶，百官皆班賀。

translations.literal: Wang Dan, Right Vice Director, served as commissioner of the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace; the relevant offices, according to precedent, held that whenever a chief minister had an auspicious celebration, the hundred officials all formed ranks to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan, Right Vice Director, also served as commissioner of the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace; by precedent, whenever a chief minister celebrated an auspicious event, the hundred officials formed ranks to congratulate.

sentences.zh: 詔以未葺攸司，其班賀權罷。

translations.literal: An edict stated that because the relevant office had not yet been repaired, the ranked congratulations were temporarily suspended.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that because the palace office was not yet repaired, the ranked congratulations were temporarily suspended.

sentences.zh: 旦赴上修宮所，特賜會，丞、郎、三司副使以上悉預。

translations.literal: When Dan presented himself at the palace under repair, a special banquet was granted; assistant directors, directors, and Three Departments vice commissioners and above all attended.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan reported at the palace site under repair, a special banquet was granted; assistant directors, directors, and Three Departments vice commissioners and above all attended.

sentences.zh: 自是宮觀使副上日皆賜會作樂。

translations.literal: From this time, on the reporting day of palace commissioners and their deputies, banquets with music were always granted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, on the reporting day of palace commissioners and their deputies, banquets with music were always provided.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，太保、平章事王旦為太尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi, Grand Guardian and Commissioner with Equal Authority Wang Dan became Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianxi, Grand Guardian and Commissioner with Equal Authority Wang Dan was appointed Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 國朝以來，三公不兼宰相，無赴上儀。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the dynasty, the Three Dukes did not concurrently hold chief minister, and there was no ceremony for presenting oneself at court.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty's founding, the Three Dukes had not concurrently served as chief minister, and no court-reporting ceremony existed for them.

sentences.zh: 特詔有司詳定，就尚書省赴上，百官班迎，宰相而下悉集。

translations.literal: A special edict ordered the relevant offices to examine and fix it in detail; he presented himself at the Department of State Affairs, the hundred officials formed ranks to welcome him, and from the chief minister down all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict ordered the relevant offices to define the rite; he reported at the Department of State Affairs, the hundred officials formed ranks to welcome him, and everyone from the chief minister down assembled.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫、中丞、知雜、三院御史皆僚屬送上，判案三道。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief, Vice Censor-in-Chief, Commissioner in Charge of Miscellaneous Affairs, and censors of the three bureaus were all subordinates who presented him; three cases were marked for approval.
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief, Vice Censor-in-Chief, Commissioner in Charge of Miscellaneous Affairs, and censors of the three bureaus, as his subordinates, presented him; three cases were marked for approval.

sentences.zh: 中丞以上，即京府尹、赤縣令、諸曹、節度、刺史、皇城、宮苑使悉集。

translations.literal: From the Vice Censor-in-Chief upward, the capital prefect, magistrates of the imperial counties, various bureau heads, military commissioners, prefects, commissioners of the Imperial City and Palace Parks—all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: From the Vice Censor-in-Chief upward, the capital prefect, magistrates of the imperial counties, bureau heads, military commissioners, prefects, and commissioners of the Imperial City and Palace Parks all assembled.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士入院日賜設，惟學士、中書舍人赴坐。

translations.literal: On the day a Hanlin academician entered the academy, a banquet was granted; only academicians and Secretariat drafters attended the seating.
translations.idiomatic: On the day a Hanlin academician entered the academy, a banquet was granted; only academicians and Secretariat drafting officials took seats.

sentences.zh: 又資政、侍讀、侍講、龍圖閣學士、直學士兼秘書監並赴上。

translations.literal: Further, Academicians of the Privy Council, Readers-in-Waiting, Expositors-in-Waiting, Dragon Diagram Hall academicians, and direct academicians concurrently holding Director of the Palace Library also presented themselves at court.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Council academicians, Readers-in-Waiting, Expositors-in-Waiting, Dragon Diagram Hall academicians, and direct academicians who concurrently held Director of the Palace Library likewise reported to court.

sentences.zh: 秘閣及兩省五品以上任三館學士、判館、修撰者，皆賜設焉。

translations.literal: For the Secretariat Pavilion and fifth-rank officials of the two administrations and above who held posts as academicians of the Three Institutes, directors of the institutes, or compilers, banquets were all granted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Secretariat Pavilion and fifth rank or above in the two administrations who served as Three Institutes academicians, institute directors, or compilers likewise received banquets.

sentences.zh: 朝省集議，前代不載其儀。

translations.literal: Assemblies for deliberation at the provincial offices—previous ages did not record their ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Assemblies for deliberation at the provincial offices were not recorded in earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 宋初，刑政典禮之事當集議者，先下詔都省，省吏以告當議之官，悉集都堂，設左、右丞于堂之東北，南向；

translations.literal: Early in Song, for matters of penal administration, canonical rites, and ceremonial affairs requiring assembly for deliberation, an edict was first sent down to the provincial offices; the provincial clerks informed the officials who should deliberate, and all assembled in the main hall; the Left and Right Assistant Directors were set in the northeast of the hall, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, when penal, canonical, or ceremonial matters required joint deliberation, an edict went first to the provincial offices; clerks summoned the designated officials to the main hall, where the Left and Right Assistant Directors sat in the northeast, facing south;

sentences.zh: 御史中丞於堂之西北，南向；

translations.literal: the Vice Censor-in-Chief in the northwest of the hall, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: the Vice Censor-in-Chief in the northwest, facing south;

sentences.zh: 尚書、侍郎于堂東廂，西向；

translations.literal: Directors and Vice Directors in the eastern wing of the hall, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: Directors and Vice Directors in the eastern wing, facing west;

sentences.zh: 兩省侍郎、常侍、給事、諫舍於堂之西廂，東向；

translations.literal: Vice Directors, Regular Attendants, Drafters, Remonstrators, and Advisers of the two administrations in the western wing of the hall, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Directors, Regular Attendants, Drafters, Remonstrators, and Advisers of the two administrations in the western wing, facing east;

sentences.zh: 知名表郎官于堂之東南，北向；

translations.literal: notable memorial drafters in the southeast of the hall, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: notable memorial drafters in the southeast, facing north;

sentences.zh: 監議御史於堂之西南，北向。

translations.literal: supervising censors in the southwest of the hall, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: supervising censors in the southwest, facing north.

sentences.zh: 又設左右司郎中、員外于左、右丞之後，三院御史於中丞之後，郎中、員外于尚書、侍郎之後，起居、司諫、正言於諫舍之後。

translations.literal: Further, the Left and Right Bureau directors and vice directors were set behind the Assistant Directors, censors of the three bureaus behind the Vice Censor-in-Chief, directors and vice directors behind the Directors and Vice Directors, and Regular Attendants, Remonstrators, and Rectifiers behind the Remonstrators and Advisers.
translations.idiomatic: Behind them sat the Left and Right Bureau directors and vice directors behind the Assistant Directors; censors of the three bureaus behind the Vice Censor-in-Chief; directors and vice directors behind the department heads; and Regular Attendants, Remonstrators, and Rectifiers behind the Remonstrators and Advisers.

sentences.zh: 如有僕射、御史大夫，即于左右丞，中丞之前。

translations.literal: If there were Vice Directors or Censors-in-Chief, they were placed before the Assistant Directors and Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: If Vice Directors or a Censor-in-Chief were present, they sat before the Assistant Directors and Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 如更有他官，即諸司三品于侍郎之南，東宮一品于尚書之前，武班二品於諫舍之南，皆重行異位。

translations.literal: If there were still other officials, then third-rank officials of the various offices south of the Vice Directors, Eastern Palace first rank before the Directors, and second-rank military officials south of the Remonstrators and Advisers—all in double rows at separate places.
translations.idiomatic: Other officials took assigned places: third-rank agency heads south of the Vice Directors; Eastern Palace first rank before the Directors; second-rank military officials south of the Remonstrators—all in double rows at separate stations.

sentences.zh: 卑者先就席。

translations.literal: The lower in rank first took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: The lower in rank took their seats first.

sentences.zh: 左、右丞升廳，省吏抗聲揖群官就坐，知名表郎官以所議事授所司奉詣左、右丞，左、右丞執卷讀訖授中丞、中丞授于尚書、侍郎，以次讀訖，復授知名表郎官。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Assistant Directors ascended the hall; provincial clerks called out loudly and bowed to urge the multitude of officials to be seated; the notable memorial drafter handed the matter under deliberation to the relevant office and brought it to the Assistant Directors; the Assistant Directors held the scroll, read it finished, and handed it to the Vice Censor-in-Chief; the Vice Censor-in-Chief handed it to the Directors and Vice Directors, who read in turn until finished, and it was handed back to the notable memorial drafter.
translations.idiomatic: The Assistant Directors ascended; clerks called out and bowed the officials to their seats. The notable memorial drafter delivered the matter to the relevant office and brought it to the Assistant Directors, who read it through and passed it to the Vice Censor-in-Chief, then to the Directors and Vice Directors in turn, and finally back to the notable memorial drafter.

sentences.zh: 將畢，左、右丞奉筆叩頭揖群官，以一副紙書所議事節署字於下，授四坐。

translations.literal: When nearly finished, the Assistant Directors held the brush, knocked their heads, and bowed to the multitude of officials; on a separate sheet they wrote the matter under deliberation and signed their names below, and handed it to the four seats.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end, the Assistant Directors took the brush, knocked their heads, bowed to the assembly, wrote the matter on a separate sheet with their signatures below, and distributed copies to the four seats.

sentences.zh: 監議御史命吏告云：「所見不同者請不署字。」

translations.literal: The supervising censor ordered a clerk to announce: 'Those whose views differ, please do not sign.'
translations.idiomatic: The supervising censor had a clerk announce: 'Those who disagree should not sign.'

sentences.zh: 以官高者為表首。

translations.literal: The official of higher rank served as head of the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The highest-ranking official led the memorial.

sentences.zh: 如止集本省官，坐如常儀，其知名表郎官、監議御史坐仍北向。

translations.literal: If only officials of one's own department assembled, seating followed the regular ceremony; the notable memorial drafter and supervising censor still sat facing north.
translations.idiomatic: When only one's own department assembled, seating followed the regular arrangement; the notable memorial drafter and supervising censor still faced north.

sentences.zh: 惟僕射以上得乘馬至都堂，他官雖同平章，事亦止屏外。

translations.literal: Only from Vice Director upward might one ride a horse to the main hall; other officials, even if concurrently Equal in Authority to the Chief Minister, still stopped outside the screen.
translations.idiomatic: Only officials from Vice Director upward might ride a horse to the main hall; others, even with the concurrent chief-minister title, still halted outside the screen.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，尚書議莊獻、莊懿太后升祔，省官帶內外制、兼三司副使承例移文不赴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao, when the Department of State Affairs deliberated enshrining the Empresses Dowager Zhuangxian and Zhuangyi, provincial officials holding inner and outer drafting posts concurrently with Three Departments vice commissioner followed precedent in sending documents and did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingdao (1033), when the Department deliberated enshrining Empresses Dowager Zhuangxian and Zhuangyi, provincial officials who concurrently held drafting posts and Three Departments vice commissioner titles sent documents under precedent and did not attend.

sentences.zh: 監議御史段少連以為官帶近職，一時之選，宜有建明，不當反自高異。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Duan Shaolian held that officials holding near-service posts were selections for the moment and ought to offer constructive views, and should not on the contrary set themselves apart as higher.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Duan Shaolian argued that holders of near-service posts were chosen for the moment and ought to offer constructive views rather than hold themselves aloof.

sentences.zh: 乃奏議事不集以違制論。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized that failure to assemble for deliberation should be prosecuted as violation of regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore memorialized that failure to attend deliberation should be prosecuted as a regulatory violation.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The throne followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 集賢校理趙良規言：「國朝故事，令敕儀制，別有學士、知制誥、待制、三司副使著位，視品與前朝異，固無在朝敘職、入省敘官之說。

translations.literal: Collator of the Hall of Assembled Talents Zhao Lianggui stated: 'According to dynastic precedent, edicts and ritual regulations separately assigned positions to academicians, drafters, recipients of Awaiting Imperial Orders, and Three Departments vice commissioners; viewing rank, they differ from the previous dynasty, and in truth there is no theory of court precedence versus provincial precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Collator Zhao Lianggui of the Hall of Assembled Talents argued: 'Dynastic precedent assigns separate positions in edicts and ritual codes to academicians, drafters, Awaiting Imperial Orders recipients, and Three Departments vice commissioners; their court rank differs from Tang practice, and there is no clear rule for court versus provincial precedence.

sentences.zh: 若全不論職，則後行員外郎兼學士，在朝立丞、郎上，入省居比、駕下；

translations.literal: If one wholly disregarded office, then a rear-row vice director concurrently holding academician would stand above assistant directors and directors at court, but below them in the provincial offices;
translations.idiomatic: If office were wholly disregarded, a rear-row vice director who concurrently served as academician would stand above assistant directors and directors at court yet below them in the provincial offices;

sentences.zh: 知制誥、待制入朝與侍郎同列，入省分廁散郎；

translations.literal: drafters and recipients of Awaiting Imperial Orders would stand in court in the same row as Vice Directors, but in the provincial offices would share latrines with unattached directors;
translations.idiomatic: drafters and Awaiting Imperial Orders recipients would rank with Vice Directors at court yet share latrines with unattached directors in the provincial offices;

sentences.zh: 員外郎任三司副使、郎中任判官，在三司為參佐，入本省為正員。

translations.literal: a vice director serving as Three Departments vice commissioner, or a director serving as judge, was a subordinate in the Three Departments but a regular official in his own department.
translations.idiomatic: a vice director serving as Three Departments vice commissioner, or a director serving as judge, was a subordinate in the Three Departments but a full regular official in his own department.

sentences.zh: 所以舊來議事，集尚書省官，帶職者不赴。

translations.literal: Therefore in former times when deliberating affairs, they assembled officials of the Department of State Affairs; those holding concurrent posts did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, deliberations at the Department of State Affairs traditionally summoned only its own officials, while those holding concurrent posts did not attend.

sentences.zh: 別詔三省悉集，則及大小兩省；

translations.literal: If a separate edict ordered all three administrations to assemble, then both the great and small two administrations were included;
translations.idiomatic: When a separate edict required all three administrations to assemble, both the senior and junior two administrations were included;

sentences.zh: 內朝官悉集，則及學士、待制、三司副使；

translations.literal: if inner-court officials were all to assemble, then academicians, recipients of Awaiting Imperial Orders, and Three Departments vice commissioners were included;
translations.idiomatic: when inner-court officials were summoned, academicians, Awaiting Imperial Orders recipients, and Three Departments vice commissioners were included;

sentences.zh: 更集他官，則諸司三品、武官二品，各次本司長官。

translations.literal: if other officials were further assembled, then third-rank officials of the various offices and second-rank military officials each followed the chief of their own office.
translations.idiomatic: if still other officials were called, third-rank agency heads and second-rank military officers each followed their own department chiefs.

sentences.zh: 故事，尚書省官帶知制誥，中書省奏班簿，是於尚書省、御史台了不著籍，故有絕曹之語。

translations.literal: By precedent, when an official of the Department of State Affairs concurrently held the title drafter, the Secretariat submitted the rank roster—thus in the Department of State Affairs and Censorate he was not entered in the register, hence the saying 'severed from the bureau.'
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, a Department official who concurrently served as drafter was listed on the Secretariat's rank roster but not registered with the Department or Censorate—hence the phrase 'severed from the bureau.'

sentences.zh: 又凡定學士、舍人、兩省著位，除先後入外，若有升降，皆特稟朝旨，豈有在朝、入省迭為高下？」

translations.literal: Further, whenever fixing the assigned positions of academicians, drafters, and the two administrations, apart from order of entry, if there were promotions or demotions, all specially reported to the court for instruction—how could there be alternation of higher and lower at court versus in the provincial offices?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, assigning positions to academicians, drafters, and the two administrations depended on order of entry and special court orders for any promotion or demotion—how could court and provincial precedence simply alternate?'

sentences.zh: 御史台、禮院詳定，久不決。

translations.literal: The Censorate and Rites Office examined and fixed it in detail, but for a long time no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate and Rites Office reviewed the matter at length but could not reach a decision for some time.

sentences.zh: 判禮院馮元等曰：「會議之文，由來非一，或出朝廷別旨，或循官司舊規。

translations.literal: Feng Yuan and others, who judged the Rites Office, said: 'Documents for assemblies have never been uniform; some issued from separate court instructions, some followed old regulations of the offices.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yuan and others, adjudicating for the Rites Office, argued: 'Assembly summons had never been uniform—some issued from separate court instructions, others followed each office's old regulations.

sentences.zh: 故集本省者，即南省官；

translations.literal: Thus when assembling officials of one's own department, that meant Southern Administration officials;
translations.idiomatic: When one's own department assembled, that meant Southern Administration officials;

sentences.zh: 集學士、兩省、台官者，容有兩制、給舍、中丞；

translations.literal: when assembling academicians, the two administrations, and Censorate officials, it might include drafters and drafters of memorials, Regular Attendants, and Vice Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: when academicians, the two administrations, and Censorate officials assembled, drafters, memorial drafters, Regular Attendants, and the Vice Censor-in-Chief might be included;

sentences.zh: 集學士、台省及諸司四品以上者，容有卿、監；

translations.literal: when assembling academicians, the Censorate and provincial offices, and officials of the fourth rank and above of the various offices, it might include directors and commissioners;
translations.idiomatic: when academicians, the Censorate and provincial offices, and fourth-rank officials and above assembled, directors and commissioners might be included;

sentences.zh: 集文武百官者，容有諸衛。

translations.literal: when assembling civil and military hundred officials, it might include the various guards.
translations.idiomatic: when civil and military officials assembled, the various guards might be included.

sentences.zh: 蓋謀事有小大，集官有等差，率系詔文，乃該餘職。

translations.literal: In general the matter to be planned had its small and great dimensions, and the officials assembled had their grades; all followed the edict text, and thus covered the remaining offices.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberations varied in scope, and summoned officials varied in rank—all according to the edict, which thereby covered the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 少連乙太常易名之細，考功覆議之常，誤謂群司普當會席，列為具奏，嬰以嚴科，遂使絕曹清列，還入本行，分局常員，略無異等。

translations.literal: Shaolian took the minor matter of the Grand Sacrifices Office changing a name in the Yi year and the routine review by the Ministry of Personnel as error, holding that all offices universally should attend the assembly seat, listing it as a full memorial, and burdening it with severe punishment—thus making officials severed from the bureau return to their original rows, dividing regular posts with scarcely any distinction of grade.
translations.idiomatic: Shaolian had treated minor matters—the Grand Sacrifices Office's Yi-year name change and the Ministry of Personnel's routine review—as if every office should always attend, listed them in a full memorial, and sought severe punishment, forcing 'severed bureau' officials back into ordinary rows with little distinction among regular posts.

sentences.zh: 請臣僚擬諡，止集南省官屬，或事緣體大，臨時敕判，兼召三省、台、寺，即依舊例。」

translations.literal: We request that when ministers deliberate posthumous titles, only Southern Administration subordinates be assembled; or if the matter by its nature were great, a temporary edict might order it, summoning concurrently the three administrations, Censorate, and courts—then follow the old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that deliberations on posthumous titles summon only Southern Administration subordinates; if the matter were exceptionally weighty, a temporary edict might additionally summon the three administrations, Censorate, and courts, following old precedent.'

sentences.zh: 御史台言：「今尚書省官任兩制者，系台省之籍，無坐曹之實。

translations.literal: The Censorate stated: 'Today when an official of the Department of State Affairs holds a drafter post, he is entered in the Censorate and provincial roster but has no reality of sitting in the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate replied: 'Today a Department official who concurrently serves as drafter is entered on the Censorate and provincial roster yet does not actually sit in the bureau.

sentences.zh: 論職官之言，正為絕曹者設，豈可受祿則系官定奉，議事則絕曹為辭？

translations.literal: Discussion of office and rank is precisely set forth for those severed from the bureau—how can one receive salary and be tied to office for fixed stipend, yet when deliberating affairs use severance from the bureau as an excuse?
translations.idiomatic: Rules on office and rank exist precisely for those severed from the bureau—how can one draw salary under a fixed office title yet plead severance from the bureau when deliberating affairs?

sentences.zh: 況王旦、王化基、趙安仁、晁迥、杜鎬、楊億皆嘗預議於尚書省。

translations.literal: Moreover Wang Dan, Wang Huaji, Zhao Anren, Chao Jiong, Du Hao, and Yang Yi all once participated in deliberation at the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Wang Dan, Wang Huaji, Zhao Anren, Chao Jiong, Du Hao, and Yang Yi had all deliberated at the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 故相李昉為主客郎中、知制誥日，屢經都省議事。

translations.literal: Former chief minister Li Fang, when he was Director of the Bureau of Receptions and drafter, repeatedly deliberated affairs at the provincial main hall.
translations.idiomatic: Former chief minister Li Fang, while Director of the Bureau of Receptions and drafter, had repeatedly deliberated at the provincial main hall.

sentences.zh: 又議大事，僕射、御史大夫入省，唯僕射至廳下馬，於今行之，所以重本省也。

translations.literal: Further, when deliberating great affairs, Vice Directors and Censors-in-Chief entered the provincial offices; only the Vice Director dismounted his horse below the hall—still practiced today—therefore to honor this department.
translations.idiomatic: When great affairs were deliberated, Vice Directors and Censors-in-Chief entered the provincial offices; only the Vice Director dismounted below the hall—a practice still observed today—to honor the department.

sentences.zh: 故都堂會議，列狀以品，就坐以官，忽此更張，恐非通理。」

translations.literal: Thus at assemblies in the main hall, they listed memorials by rank and took seats by office; suddenly to change this would likely not accord with general principle.'
translations.idiomatic: At main-hall assemblies, memorials were ordered by rank and seats by office; to overturn this abruptly would likely violate sound principle.'

sentences.zh: 禮官吳育曰：「兩奏各有未安。

translations.literal: Rites official Wu Yu said: 'Both memorials have points that are not settled.
translations.idiomatic: Rites official Wu Yu said: 'Neither proposal is fully satisfactory.

sentences.zh: 尚書省制度雖崇，亦天子之有司，在朝廷既殊班列，入有司輒易尊卑，是以朝省為彼我、官職分二事也。

translations.literal: Although the system of the Department of State Affairs is lofty, it is still the Son of Heaven's offices; at court the ranks are already distinct, yet upon entering the offices one abruptly changes superior and inferior—thus court and provincial offices become mutual parties, and office and duty are divided into two affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Department of State Affairs ranks high, it remains the emperor's bureaucracy; ranks already differ at court, yet entering the offices one suddenly reverses superior and inferior—making court and provincial offices rival camps and splitting office from duty.

sentences.zh: 兩制近職，若有事議而雲絕班不赴，非所以求至當。

translations.literal: For near-service drafters, if there were affairs to deliberate yet they said they were severed from rank and would not attend, this is not the way to seek what is most fitting.
translations.idiomatic: If near-service drafters refused attendance on grounds of severed rank when affairs required deliberation, that was no way to reach the best outcome.

sentences.zh: 且知制誥中書省奏班簿，是謂絕班。

translations.literal: Moreover the drafter's rank roster submitted by the Secretariat is what is called severed from rank.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the drafter's rank roster submitted by the Secretariat is what 'severed rank' means.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士亦知制誥，不絕班簿。

translations.literal: Hanlin academicians also hold the title drafter but are not severed from the rank roster.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academicians also hold the drafter title but are not severed from the rank roster.

sentences.zh: 此因循之制，非確據也。

translations.literal: This is a system carried on by inertia, not firm evidence.
translations.idiomatic: That was inertia, not firm precedent.

sentences.zh: 縱絕班有例，而絕官無聞，一人命書，三省連判，而都無所系，止為奉錢，豈命官之禮？

translations.literal: Even if severance from rank had precedent, severance from office was unheard of; one person's appointment document was jointly marked by the three administrations, yet he was tied to none of them, receiving only salary—was this the ritual of appointing an office?
translations.idiomatic: Even if severed rank had precedent, severed office did not; one man's appointment was countersigned by all three administrations yet tied to none, receiving only salary—is that how offices are appointed?

sentences.zh: 今取典故中最明一事，足以質定。

translations.literal: Now take the clearest single precedent from the classics, sufficient to determine the matter by evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Take the clearest single precedent, sufficient to settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 祥符五年僕射上事儀：絕班之官，別頭贊引，不與本省官同在迎班。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xiangfu, the ceremony for a Vice Director presenting himself: officials severed from rank had a separate lead in announcement and guidance, not in the same welcoming line as officials of one's own department.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth year of Xiangfu ceremony for a Vice Director's presentation required officials severed from rank to have a separate usher and not share the welcoming line with their own department.

sentences.zh: 請凡會議，省官帶近職者，別作一行而坐，自為序列，非以相壓。

translations.literal: We request that whenever deliberating, provincial officials holding near-service posts sit in a separate row by themselves, forming their own sequence, not to press down on others.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that at deliberations, provincial officials with near-service posts sit in a separate row forming their own sequence, not to dominate others.

sentences.zh: 若招兩制、台省、諸司、諸衛官畢集，則各從其類，自作一行，書議如其位次。」

translations.literal: If drafters, Censorate and provincial offices, various offices, and guard officials are all summoned, then each follows its category, each forming its own row, and the written deliberation follows their place in order.'
translations.idiomatic: If drafters, Censorate and provincial officials, various agencies, and guards are all summoned, each category forms its own row, and the written deliberation follows their proper order.'

sentences.zh: 詔尚書省議事，應帶職官三司副使以上並不赴，如遇集議大事，令赴，別設坐次。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that for deliberations at the Department of State Affairs, concurrent officials from Three Departments vice commissioner upward should not attend; when great deliberations required attendance, they should attend with separate seating.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ruled that at Department deliberations, concurrent officials from Three Departments vice commissioner upward need not attend; when major deliberations required them, they attended with separate seating.

sentences.zh: 是歲，紫宸、垂拱殿刊石為百官表位。

translations.literal: That year, stone was carved at Zichen and Chuigong halls for the ranked positions of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: That year, ranked positions for the hundred officials were carved in stone at the Zichen and Chuigong halls.

sentences.zh: 三司使，內朝班學士右，獨立石位；

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Three Departments: in the inner-court rank, academicians to the right, with a separate stone position;
translations.idiomatic: For the Three Departments commissioner: in the inner-court formation, academicians stood to the right with a separate stone marker;

sentences.zh: 門外，亦班其上。

translations.literal: outside the gate, also ranked above them.
translations.idiomatic: outside the gate, likewise ranked above them.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，御史台、太常禮院詳定臣僚禦路上馬之制：近上臣僚及北使到闕，並於禦路上行馬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, the Censorate and Court of Imperial Sacrifices Rites Office examined and fixed in detail the regulations for officials mounting horses on the Imperial Way: high-ranking officials and envoys from the north arriving at court all traveled on horseback on the Imperial Way.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xining (1069), the Censorate and Court of Imperial Sacrifices Rites Office defined regulations for mounting horses on the Imperial Way: senior officials and northern envoys arriving at court all rode along the Imperial Way.

sentences.zh: 中書樞密院執政官、宣徽院、御史中丞、知雜御史、左右金吾、攝事官清道者，導從呵止依舊式，其三司副使以上亦許出節。

translations.literal: Chief ministers of the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs, commissioners of the Palace Domestic Service, Vice Censor-in-Chief, Commissioner in Charge of Miscellaneous Affairs, Left and Right Golden Guard, and commissioners acting with clear passage—guides and shouts to halt followed the old form; Three Departments vice commissioners and above were also permitted to display insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers of the Secretariat and Bureau, Palace Domestic Service commissioners, Vice Censor-in-Chief, Commissioner in Charge of Miscellaneous Affairs, Left and Right Golden Guard, and acting commissioners with clear passage kept the old escort and shouting rules; Three Departments vice commissioners and above might also display insignia.

sentences.zh: 正任觀察使以上與合出節臣僚，並許自宣德門外至天漢橋北禦路上行馬，如從賀出入及宗室內庭諸宮院車騎，並不在此限。

translations.literal: Regular appointees of military commissioner and above together with officials permitted to display insignia were all allowed to ride on the Imperial Way from outside Xuande Gate to north of Tianhan Bridge; such as going out for congratulations or the imperial clan's inner palaces and various palace compounds with carriages and riders were not within this limit.
translations.idiomatic: Regular appointees of military commissioner and above, together with officials permitted insignia, might ride the Imperial Way from outside Xuande Gate to north of Tianhan Bridge; processions for congratulations and imperial-clan inner palaces were excepted.

sentences.zh: 御史台又言：「舊制：百官台參、辭謝臣僚于朝堂，先赴三院御史幕次，又赴中丞幕次，得以體按老疾。

translations.literal: The Censorate further stated: 'Old regulations: when the hundred officials attended the provincial offices or officials presented thanks and farewell at the audience hall, they first went to the three bureaus' censor screens, then to the Vice Censor-in-Chief's screen, and could thereby rest according to age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate added: 'Under the old rules, when the hundred officials attended the provincial offices or presented thanks and farewell at the audience hall, they first visited the three bureaus' censor screens, then the Vice Censor-in-Chief's screen, where age and illness could be accommodated.

sentences.zh: 今止于御史廳一員對拜，不惟有失舊儀，兼恐不能公共參驗。

translations.literal: Today it stops at a single censor in the Censorate hall exchanging bows, which not only loses the old ceremony but also likely cannot jointly verify in public.
translations.idiomatic: Today only a single censor in the Censorate hall exchanges bows—not only losing the old ceremony but likely preventing joint public verification.

sentences.zh: 請如舊制朝堂拜揖，遇放常朝，即詣御史台。」

translations.literal: We request the old system of bows in the audience hall; when regular audience was canceled, then proceed to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to restore bows in the audience hall, proceeding to the Censorate only when regular audience was canceled.'

sentences.zh: 已而詔宰臣、親王、使相、兩府、宣徽使，遇入樞密院門，許至從南第二門外上下馬。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward an edict ordered that chief ministers, imperial princes, commissioners with chief-minister status, the two administrations, and Palace Domestic Service commissioners, when entering the Bureau of Military Affairs gate, might mount and dismount outside the second gate south of the followers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon allowed chief ministers, imperial princes, chief-minister commissioners, the two administrations, and Palace Domestic Service commissioners to mount and dismount outside the second gate south of the followers when entering the Bureau gate.

sentences.zh: 又詔：宰臣上馬，樞密院次之，諸司又次之，左、右丞上下馬處並同兩省侍郎。

translations.literal: Further edict: chief ministers mounted horses first, the Bureau of Military Affairs next, the various offices next; the places for Left and Right Assistant Directors to mount and dismount were the same as for Vice Directors of the two administrations.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict set mounting order: chief ministers first, then the Bureau, then other offices; the Left and Right Assistant Directors mounted and dismounted at the same places as the two administrations' Vice Directors.

sentences.zh: 御史台言：「左丞蒲宗孟、右丞王安禮賀僕射上尚書省，於都堂下馬。

translations.literal: The Censorate stated: 'Left Assistant Director Pu Zongmeng and Right Assistant Director Wang Anli congratulated the Vice Director on presenting himself at the Department of State Affairs and dismounted at the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate reported: 'Left Assistant Director Pu Zongmeng and Right Assistant Director Wang Anli congratulated the Vice Director at the Department and dismounted at the main hall.

sentences.zh: 按左、右丞上下馬於本廳。

translations.literal: According to regulations, Left and Right Assistant Directors mount and dismount at their own hall.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations required Assistant Directors to mount and dismount at their own hall.

sentences.zh: 請付有司推治。」

translations.literal: We request that the relevant offices investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: We ask the relevant offices to investigate and punish.'

sentences.zh: 安禮爭論上前，以為今日置左、右丞為執政官，不應有厚薄。

translations.literal: Anli argued before the emperor that today the Left and Right Assistant Directors are established as chief executive officials and should not be treated with partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anli argued before the emperor that Assistant Directors were now chief executive officials and should not be treated unequally.

sentences.zh: 左、右丞於都堂上下馬自此始。

translations.literal: From this time Left and Right Assistant Directors mounted and dismounted at the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: From this time Assistant Directors mounted and dismounted at the main hall.

sentences.zh: 尋詔執政官退朝上馬，宰臣于樞密院，余於隔門外。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered that after chief executive officials withdrew from audience and mounted horses, chief ministers did so at the Bureau of Military Affairs, the rest outside the partition gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict required chief executive officials after audience to mount at the Bureau for chief ministers and outside the partition gate for others.

sentences.zh: 都堂聚議退，左丞于門下侍郎廳，右丞于中書侍郎廳。

translations.literal: When assemblies at the main hall for deliberation adjourned, the Left Assistant Director did so at the Gatehouse Vice Director's hall, the Right Assistant Director at the Secretariat Vice Director's hall.
translations.idiomatic: After main-hall deliberations adjourned, the Left Assistant Director mounted at the Gatehouse Vice Director's hall and the Right at the Secretariat Vice Director's hall.

sentences.zh: 品官詣尚書省上下馬依雜壓，大中大夫以上就第一貯廊，監察御史以上就過道，諸六曹尚書、侍郎即大中大夫以上就本廳，監察御史以上就客位，餘並過道門外。

translations.literal: Officials of rank mounting and dismounting at the Department of State Affairs followed the miscellaneous precedence; Grand Masters of the Palace and above stopped at the first storage corridor, Supervising Censors and above at the passageway; all Six Bureaus Directors and Vice Directors who were Grand Masters of the Palace and above stopped at their own hall, Supervising Censors and above at the guest seat, the rest all outside the passageway gate.
translations.idiomatic: Ranked officials mounting at the Department followed miscellaneous precedence: Palace Grand Masters and above at the first storage corridor, Supervising Censors and above at the passageway; Six Bureaus Directors and Vice Directors at Grand Master rank or above at their own hall, Supervising Censors and above at the guest seat, others outside the passageway gate.

sentences.zh: 政和朝參臣僚上馬次序：俟皇城門開，樞密入，次三省執政官，次一品二品文臣觕、六曹侍郎、殿中監、開封尹、大司成、侍從官、兩省，次百官，御史台編欄以次入。

translations.literal: Order of mounting horses for officials attending audience in the Zhenghe era: after the Imperial City gate opened, the Bureau entered first, next chief executive officials of the three administrations, next first- and second-rank civil officials in coarse dress, Six Bureaus Vice Directors, Director of the Palace Directorate, Kaifeng prefect, Grand Director of Studies, attendants, and the two administrations, next the hundred officials, with the Censorate arranging columns to enter in order.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenghe, mounting order at audience was: after the Imperial City gate opened, the Bureau entered first, then three-administration chief executives, then first- and second-rank civil officials in coarse dress, Six Bureaus Vice Directors, Palace Directorate director, Kaifeng prefect, Grand Director of Studies, attendants, and the two administrations, then the hundred officials, with the Censorate arranging entry by column.

sentences.zh: 其宰相罷政，韓琦以司徒、節度判相州，曾公亮以司空、節度為集禧觀使，王安石以觀文殿大學士、吏部尚書知江甯府。

translations.literal: When chief ministers left office: Han Qi as Grand Mentor and military commissioner judged Xiangzhou; Zeng Gongliang as Grand Guardian and military commissioner served as commissioner of the Jixi Palace; Wang Anshi as Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and prefect of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: When chief ministers left office: Han Qi served as Grand Mentor and military commissioner judging Xiangzhou; Zeng Gongliang as Grand Guardian and military commissioner of the Jixi Palace; Wang Anshi as Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, Director of Personnel, and Jiangning prefect.

sentences.zh: 曹佾以中書令、節度充景靈宮使，韓絳以觀文殿大學士、吏部侍郎知大名府，致仕太師文彥博來朝，其大朝會班位儀物如之。

translations.literal: Cao Yi as Director of the Secretariat and military commissioner served as commissioner of the Jingling Palace; Han Jiang as Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture and Vice Director of Personnel was prefect of Daming; retired Grand Preceptor Wen Yanbo came to court—their great audience ranks, formation positions, and regalia were as before.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi as Director of the Secretariat and military commissioner headed the Jingling Palace; Han Jiang as Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture and Vice Director of Personnel governed Daming; retired Grand Preceptor Wen Yanbo attended court—all retaining their great-audience rank, position, and regalia.

sentences.zh: 吳育以觀文殿大學士、吏部尚書為西太一宮使，大朝會綴中書、門下班而已。

translations.literal: Wu Yu as Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture and Director of Personnel served as commissioner of the Western Supreme Unity Palace; at great audience he merely followed the Secretariat and Chancellery rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yu as Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture and Director of Personnel headed the Western Supreme Unity Palace; at great audience he merely followed the Secretariat and Chancellery formation.

sentences.zh: 自是，舊相按例重輕以特旨行之。

translations.literal: From this time, former chief ministers followed precedent of heavy and light according to special edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, former chief ministers' precedence followed special edicts weighing each case.

sentences.zh: 治平四年，御史台言：「慶曆中，有詔詳定武臣出節呵引之制：節度使在尚書下，三節。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiping, the Censorate stated: 'In the Qingli era there was an edict examining and fixing in detail the regulations for military officials displaying insignia and ushering: a military commissioner ranked below the Director and displayed three insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhiping (1067), the Censorate reported: 'During Qingli an edict had defined military officials' insignia and escorts: a military commissioner ranked below the Director and displayed three insignia.

sentences.zh: 節度觀察留後在諸行侍郎下，兩節。

translations.literal: A military commissioner, observation commissioner, or acting commissioner ranked below the various bureau vice directors and displayed two insignia.
translations.idiomatic: A military commissioner, observation commissioner, or acting commissioner ranked below bureau vice directors and displayed two insignia.

sentences.zh: 觀察使在中書舍人下，諸衛大將軍、防禦，團練使在大卿監下，內客省使比諸司大卿，景福殿使比將作監，引進使比庶子，在防禦使上，以上各一節。

translations.literal: An observation commissioner ranked below a Secretariat drafter; various guard grand generals, defense commissioners, and training commissioners ranked below grand directors and commissioners; the Inner Reception commissioner compared to grand directors of various offices, the Jingfu Hall commissioner to the Directorate of Imperial Works, the Presentation commissioner to the Palace Son—above defense commissioners; all the above displayed one insignia each.
translations.idiomatic: An observation commissioner ranked below a Secretariat drafter; guard grand generals, defense commissioners, and training commissioners below grand directors; the Inner Reception commissioner equaled grand directors, the Jingfu Hall commissioner the Directorate of Imperial Works, the Presentation commissioner the Palace Son—all above defense commissioners and each displaying one insignia.

sentences.zh: 諸州刺史、諸衛將軍在少卿監下，宣慶、四方館使比少卿，宣政、昭宣、閣門使比司天監少監，諸衛將軍上，皇城使以下諸司使比郎中，客省、引進、閣門副使比員外郎，樞密都承旨在司天少監下、閣門使上，副都承旨在閣門使下，樞密副承旨、諸房副承旨在諸司使下，以上並兩人呵引。

translations.literal: Various prefects and guard generals ranked below vice directors and commissioners; Xuanqing and Four Directions commissioners compared to vice directors; Xuanzheng, Zhaoxuan, and Gatehouse commissioners compared to the Vice Director of the Directorate of Astronomy; above guard generals; Imperial City commissioners and various office commissioners below directors; Reception, Presentation, and Gatehouse vice commissioners below vice directors; Bureau chief and deputy chief commissioners below the Directorate Vice Director and above Gatehouse commissioners; deputy chief commissioners of the various bureaus below various office commissioners—all with two ushers shouting.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and guard generals ranked below vice directors; Xuanqing and Four Directions commissioners equaled vice directors; Xuanzheng, Zhaoxuan, and Gatehouse commissioners equaled the Directorate of Astronomy vice director, above guard generals; Imperial City and other commissioners below directors; Reception, Presentation, and Gatehouse vice commissioners below vice directors; Bureau chiefs below the Astronomy vice director and above Gatehouse commissioners; bureau deputy chiefs below office commissioners—all with two shouting ushers.

sentences.zh: 當時已施行矣，而皇祐編敕刪去此制，請復舉行。」

translations.literal: At that time it had already been implemented, yet the Huangyou compiled statutes deleted this regulation; we request that it be restored and implemented again.'
translations.idiomatic: That system had already been in force, but the Huangyou compiled statutes deleted it; we ask that it be restored and enforced again.'
